title: Transparency-log segment — /ct/{n}.json and /ct/latest.json
description:
One segment of the append-only certificate transparency log. Structure for v1 is a flat signed append-only log plus checkpoints (CERT-034 default; a Merkle upgrade would add an inclusion-proof field additively — URS §21 OPEN-37). Closed segments hold exactly 10000 entries and are chained by hash; `/ct/latest.json` is the OPEN segment in the identical shape (FS08-111).

Entries carry hash, type, kind, reference and timestamp and NOTHING ELSE — no names, no emails, no subject data. That is what makes the log GDPR-compatible by content and therefore immutable forever, including through an erasure request (CERT-031, CERT-045).

At P-M2 the log is exactly one committed file, `ct/0.json` at the website repository root, appended by pull request; CI rejects any diff that edits or deletes an existing entry, which makes append-only a mechanical property rather than a promise (FS08-113, VS-28). A revocation or status change is a NEW entry whose `ref` is the ORIGINAL entry's hash — the log never edits (CERT-033).

x-psn.producer: P-M2: operator script via PR (VS-27/VS-28) · P-M3: ct-publish authors, index-build writes

segment.description: Segment number. Segment 0 is the P-M2 committed file and is carried forward unchanged at P-M3 so v0 entries stay verifiable (FS08-113).

startSeq.description: Global sequence number of this segment's first entry. Sequence is global and monotonic across segments.

prevSegmentSha256.description: SHA-256 of the previous segment document, or null for segment 0. Re-walking these hashes must reproduce the chain — divergence pages ops (FS08-114/135).

generatedAt.description: Present on the open segment (`latest.json`). A CLOSED segment is frozen byte-for-byte the moment it fills, so it deliberately carries no regeneration timestamp — its immutability is the point.

source.description: Which plane produced this artifact. `sample` and `fixture` declare a NON-PRODUCTION plane: every page that renders such an artifact is labelled sample, and a production deployment refuses to serve it (FS-10 §2 v0 note; the edge route answers `sandbox_artifact_on_prod`). `registry-v0` is the P-M2 production source of record — the curated registry repository the index is built from. Optional, and its absence asserts nothing: an artifact whose body cannot carry the label borrows the plane's declaration from `/registry/index/meta.json`. The enum widens additively when the P-M3 producer takes a value of its own.

closed.description: True once the segment reached its fixed entry count and was frozen.

entry.description: One log entry. `ref` is explicitly REQUIRED and nullable rather than optional, so an issue entry states plainly that it references nothing — a missing key and a null must not be distinguishable in an audit.

h.description: For `issue`: SHA-256 of the compact JWS string (CERT-030). For `revoke`/`status`: SHA-256 of the revocation/status entry payload — at v0 that payload is THIS entry's own members other than `seq` and `h`, serialised as RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON, `{"kind":"revoke","ref":"<the original entry's h>","ts":"<RFC 3339>","typ":"<family>"}`, with `h` the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes. It is not a separately signed object: a signed revocation family is P-M3, and the entry's own bytes are what exists at v0. `seq` is excluded because the log assigns it at append time — hashing it would make an entry's identity depend on where it landed, and would make every revocation trivially distinct, emptying the distinct-hash rule that catches one revocation logged twice. So `h` and `ref` are never equal: a revocation is a NEW object (CERT-033), not a second pointer at the object it revokes.

typ.description: JWS family — the first five values are the frozen certificate types (FS-00 §6.4), the last two the other signed families the log records: the entitlement record published at its own URL and the log's own checkpoint, both CT-appended by the v0 operator script (FS08-113, VS-27). A family is not personal data; no subject field ever enters this log.

ref.description: The ORIGINAL entry's hash for `revoke`/`status`; null for `issue` (CERT-033).
